# Compound Growth

Compound growth happens when the returns an investment earns are reinvested, so that future returns are earned on a larger and larger balance. Over long periods this snowball effect can matter more than the original amount invested, which is why starting early helps.

## A simple example

If you invest one thousand dollars and earn seven percent a year, you have one thousand seventy dollars after a year. In the second year you earn seven percent on the larger amount, and the growth keeps building on itself year after year.
